tagline: Find unmanaged devices at the edge — and learn to find more.
lore: Argos, Odysseus’s dog, who knew his master after twenty years by the smallest signs — here he recognises the devices at your network edge from their fingerprints, and learns to recognise more.
problem: Cameras, controllers, printers, firewalls and lab gear sit at the network edge with no agent, no CMDB entry and no owner. Tenable often sees them in banners, certificates and service output — but nobody turns that evidence into an inventory.
does: Argos is four cooperating agents. One confirms known devices from a detection registry; one finds the plugins on each confirmed host that carry the device's name; one sweeps those plugins across the estate and proposes new detections; one runs the loop and keeps a ledger of everything tested. You approve at two gates: tagging devices, and adding detections to the registry.

glance.caption: Argos's At a glance on a 128-asset lab: 8 IoT / OT devices confirmed by the registry, 6 of them with critical findings; 4 detections proposed for the registry from 8 carrier plugins; 6 of the 7 identity signals discovery depends on are present in the scan data.

capabilities: known devices matched by plugin, plugin name or output — the registry grows as you approve new detections.
device type, network-card vendor (OUI), local-network service announcements (mDNS) and certificates find devices the registry doesn't know yet.
host by host, the plugins whose name or output carries the device term.
a device term found in a carrier plugin on enough assets (at least 2, rising with the size of the estate) becomes a proposed detection — confirm, cross-reference or new.
critical, high and KEV findings and AES for each device.
a QA ledger of every plugin-term combination tested, and which of the seven identity signals your scans collect.
Gate 1 tags devices Asset Inventory : <facet>: <device>; Gate 2 adds approved detections to the registry, exportable.
how: Argos reads findings and plugin output in your local navi.db; nothing changes until you approve. If your scans are all credentialed agent or SSH scans of servers, the identity signals are absent and the squad finds little — the page says so instead of guessing. Tags go through navi behind the write gate and a confirm.
who: OT and IoT security teams who need an inventory they can defend, network teams hunting the unmanaged edge, and VM teams extending coverage beyond agents.
better: Argos's device tags share Linnaeus's Asset Inventory scheme, so classified devices can be owned (Ownership) and calibrated (Criticality Calibration); single candidate tags (IoT : <name>) feed Exposure Score's exposure factor. Automation re-applies the device tags on its schedule.
cta: Let Argos watch the gate — and learn every device that walks through it.
